title: Discovery questions that reveal risk tolerance
objectives: Ask the five discovery questions in a natural conversation.
Spot who the real decision-maker is.
Record the answers in the client file.
body_md:
- "What is this money for, and when will you need it?"
- "Have you invested before? What happened during the last market fall?"
- "If this investment fell 20% next year, what would you do?"
- "Who else in the family is involved in money decisions?"
- "Which investments do you already hold, including EPF, PPF, FDs and property?"

> **Investor takeaway:** Good advice starts with your goals and your comfort with risk, not with the best-performing fund.
example: You ask, 'What happened during the last market fall?' The client says, 'I stopped my SIP for a year.' You note low tolerance and plan a more conservative mix with a clear fall-time conversation.
say: If this investment fell 20% next year, what would you do?
Who else in the family is involved in money decisions?
never: You're comfortable with risk, aren't you?
Just tick the form, I'll pick the fund.

talk_track.title: Five discovery questions
talk_track.text: Here are five discovery questions every sales conversation should include. One: what is this money for, and when will you need it? Two: have you invested before, and what happened in the last market fall? Their answer tells you more about risk tolerance than any questionnaire. Three: if this investment fell 20% next year, what would you do? Four: who else in the family is involved in money decisions? Often the real decision-maker isn't in the room. Five: what do you already hold, including EPF, PPF, fixed deposits and property? Talk-track: "Before we talk about any fund, let's understand what this money is for and when you'll need it."

check.why: Past behaviour in a fall says more about tolerance than any questionnaire.
